messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redis-availability severity=P1 — 80% of API requests are returning 5xx. https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC12345

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 triggered. Notifying on-call. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> dba -> runtime.

alice (oncall): acked. I'm looking. seeing spike in 5xx and a bunch of Redis errors in the frontend logs.

alice (oncall): logs: ```[2026-06-01T12:07:31Z] ERROR redis-client: ERR max number of clients reached
[2026-06-01T12:07:32Z] WARN request-handler: cache.set failed, falling back to db write
[2026-06-01T12:07:33Z] ERROR api: downstream error: db connection pool exhausted```

bob (runtime): I'm tailing kube logs for redis-main-0/1/2. Sentinels are reporting failover attempts. latency to master pod jumped to 200-400ms before connections drop.

maya (sre): looks like a failover flapping + connection storm. Could be clients not closing connections during failover. Are we seeing lots of CLOSE_WAIT?

alice (oncall): yes, `ss -s` on redis node shows many sockets in TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT. Also p99 latency for token-generation API up to 2.4s. Customers reporting timeouts.

ryan (dba): getting alerts from Postgres too — numbackends is high and pgbouncer queue length increased. Secondary impact: backend write requests that fall back to DB are saturating pgbouncer.

carol (next-oncall): ok please summarize when hijandoff happens, I can take over escalation to accounts if needed.

alice (oncall): immediate plan: 1) stop non-critical background workers that hammer cache 
2) reduce web app concurrency on appfleet -> free DB connections 3) try to reduce redis client count by rolling redis clients (gracefully restart a few web pods)

bob (runtime): I can roll web pods in the canary set to force client reconnects (graceful). That should drop stale connections. Will do 2 pods at a time.

ops-bot: Executing: kubectl scale deployment/web-workers --replicas=0 (background workers paused)

alice (oncall): paused background workers. API 5xx rate dropped from 80% -> 42% in last 45s.

bob (runtime): rolling two web pods now... logs show clients reconnecting; redis open_fds decreasing from ~9200 -> 4300 on master.

ryan (dba): pgbouncer_queue now down from 110 -> 18. Still high but improving. Consider temporary bump to pgbouncer pool_size if we need more headroom.

maya (sre): can we set a short-term rate limit at the edge for heavy endpoints (bulk-sync, analytics)? That would reduce load quickly.

alice (oncall): edge rate limiting rule pushed for /v1/bulk-sync -> 10r/s per token. Throttling in effect. 5xx down to 18% and latency p95 dropped.

bob (runtime): Redis master is healthy but replicas lagging. Sentinel had 2 leader elections in last 10m. I suspect network flapping between nodes in that availability zone. Initiating a rolling restart of redis-statefulset to stabilize leader election.

ryan (dba): small risk: restart will cause another brief failover; weigh cost vs ongoing client storm. If web pods are reconnecting fine, restart should be OK.

alice (oncall): agree. we'll coordinate: keep background workers paused, maintain reduced concurrency, restart redis one pod at a time, wait for replication catchup.

bob (runtime): restarting redis-main-2 now. watch mastership changes.

incident-bot: pagerduty: INC12345 status=acknowledged by alice (oncall) at 2026-06-01T12:10:02Z

alice (oncall): manual mitigation in progress. I will post a short customer-impact note to #support and paste in status page draft.

alice (oncall): STATUS PAGE DRAFT: "We are investigating an issue affecting cache layer (Redis) that is causing increased errors and latency for some API requests. We are mitigating by throttling heavy endpoints and restarting cache nodes. Service impact reducing. Updates every 15m."

carol (next-oncall): I'll help coordinate customer comms once we have stable metrics for 10m.

bob (runtime): restart complete for redis-main-2; replicas caught up. master changed once during restart, then stabilized. open_fds now ~3200 and maxclients errors stopped popping.

alice (oncall): 5xx now 6% (from 80%). p95 latency back near normal. DB queue length down to 4.

ryan (dba): I'm going to increase pgbouncer max_client_conn by 20% as a short-term guard. Will revert after peak. Doing that now.

ops-bot: pgbouncer: updated pool_size from 100 -> 120 (applied).

alice (oncall): PG numbackends stabilized. No more immediate saturation.

maya (sre): next steps: 1) keep background workers off for 15m, 2) monitor for any sentinel flapping (watchdog alert), 3) add a client-side reconnect backoff to reduce simultaneous reconnect storms during failover, 4) follow-up runbook update to include throttle-by-feature plan.

alice (oncall): also file a post-incident note on root cause: likely AZ network packet loss causing sentinel elections + client reconnect storm; need long-term fix: move redis nodes to spread across subnets or enable client backoff.

carol (next-oncall): taking over the thread at 12:22Z for final checks and customer comms. summary for next oncall: incident resolved to mitigation state; background workers paused; pgbouncer bumped; redis restarted and stable; watch for recurrence.

incident-bot: pagerduty: INC12345 status=resolved by alice (oncall) at 2026-06-01T12:27:00Z (note: resolved means mitigated, follow-up required)

carol (next-oncall): acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor for the next 30m and coordinate the postmortem.

alice (oncall): thanks team. I'll open the postmortem ticket and tag db/runtime/sre. Quick notes attached to incident: mitigations, timeline, customer impact estimate: ~12% of active users saw errors for ~9 minutes at peak.

bob (runtime): suggest adding circuit-breaker in client library to prevent full reconnect storms on failover.

ryan (dba): will look into pgbouncer tuning for connection storms and write a short doc.

maya (sre): good job. closing monitoring loop: set temporary alert suppression for repeated PagerDuty flaps for this incident window to avoid noise.

carol (next-oncall): passing to postmortem owner. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
